tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what agents-auto-research is: an autonomous quantitative research loop that drives an LLM-powered cycle of plan thesis -> research -> compile -> backtest -> iterate across strategy families like EMA and ORB. The README covers setup, environment variables, and the high-level architecture map you will see expanded in the next steps. CLAUDE.md is included alongside as the project's operating discipline — it documents the non-negotiable rules, error policy, and architecture conventions that the rest of the code is built around.

tour.title: Controller Entry Point
tour.description: autoresearch_controller.py is the main state-machine loop and CLI entry point that drives one strategy family through launch, resume, halted-recovery, and builder-pipeline transitions. It is the highest fan-out file in the project (14 outbound imports) and the apex of the dependency tree — every other layer you will tour hangs off this controller. Reading it gives a bird's-eye view of the research loop's lifecycle.
tour.languageLesson: Python state machines are commonly expressed as plain functions dispatching on a status string rather than a formal FSM library — the loop body reads a state file, picks the next action, mutates state, and persists. This keeps resume semantics trivial: re-running the same command always picks up from the last persisted state.

tour.title: Orchestration Helpers and Shared State
tour.description: The controller from Step 2 delegates state transitions to autoresearch_orchestration.py — activating builder configs, resuming halted theses, archiving blockers, and choosing the next action. autoresearch_state.py owns reading and writing the on-disk run state, while autoresearch_constants.py centralizes paths, model ids, thresholds, and env-var names that the controller and helpers all share. Together these three form the orchestration substrate of the loop.

tour.title: Agent Plane: Public API and Conductor
tour.description: Now we descend into the Agent Plane that powers the 'research' phase of the loop. agent_orchestrator.py is the public async/sync entry point for diagnostic analysis, web research, and thesis generation. research_conductor.py is the top-level conductor that drives multi-round sub-agent dialogue with state, tracing, and validation — it is what the controller actually calls when a thesis needs more research.

tour.title: Sub-Agents and LLM Plumbing
tour.description: Below the conductor sit the actual sub-agent implementations and the OpenAI call layer. research_subagents.py implements the analyst (Python execution, market data, backtest DB) and web researcher with manifest, artifact, and failure-budget plumbing. agent_openai_calls.py is the OpenAI wrapper with retry and token tracking, and agent_infra.py provides the shared client and retry infrastructure that every agent relies on.

tour.title: Compiler Pipeline: Thesis to Runnable Strategy
tour.description: Once research produces a thesis, the compiler pipeline turns it into runnable code. compiler_pipeline.py is the barrel that re-exports the phases: operationalize first translates the thesis into structured config changes, then builder invokes the Codex CLI to fill in any missing strategy primitives, manages workspace snapshots, validates generated configs, and promotes successful builds. This is the bridge between LLM output and executable strategy code.

tour.title: Backtest Experiment Runner
tour.description: After compilation the loop runs a backtest. autoresearch_experiment.py invokes the backtest subprocess, parses the result JSON, derives trade analyses, and persists records to the BacktestRunDB defined in backtest_run_db.py. This is where 'did the thesis actually work?' gets answered — the metrics produced here feed back into the controller's next-action decision in Step 3.

tour.title: Strategy Plugin System
tour.description: Strategies are pluggable. strategies/base.py defines the Strategy protocol, BaseStrategy helper, FamilyDirnames layout, and the @register decorator that populates the global STRATEGIES dict. strategies/__init__.py discovers and registers each family on import. This registry is what the experiment runner in Step 7 looks up to find the EMA or ORB implementation by name.
tour.languageLesson: Python plugin registries commonly use a @register class decorator that mutates a module-level dict at import time. Just importing the package's __init__.py is enough to populate the registry — no manual wiring needed at call sites.

tour.title: Concrete Strategy Families: EMA and ORB
tour.description: Two concrete strategy families demonstrate the plugin contract. strategies/ema/strategy.py runs the full EMA backtest pipeline — data load, filters, signal generation, exit simulation, metrics, and event logging — and exposes the EMAStrategy plugin class. strategies/orb/strategy.py wires the Opening Range Breakout contract, defaults, prompt, research spec, validator, and runner into the same Strategy protocol from Step 8.

tour.title: Trace and Telemetry
tour.description: Every research round emits structured telemetry. trace_sdk.py defines TraceEvent, the JsonLineTraceExporter, the OpenTelemetry provider, and the begin_* helpers that every layer above uses to record spans. agent_token_usage.py is the round-level token ledger with budget warnings, provider inference, and trace emission — it is how the post-run scripts/token_audit.py CLI can group costs by model, agent, or job. autoresearch_logging.py is the most-imported file in the project (31 inbound edges), giving every module a consistent structured logger.

tour.title: Improvement Loop
tour.description: After a successful round, the improvement loop can polish the generated code. improvement_halo.py shells out to the external `halo` CLI for code-improvement passes and parses its output back into the loop. This is an optional but important post-round phase that sits between a passing backtest and the next thesis cycle.

tour.title: Configuration and CI
tour.description: The tour ends with the project's outer shell. .env.example documents every required environment variable — data root, VPS SSH targets, Discord webhooks, git repo — that the controller and VPS runner read at startup. pyproject.toml pins dependencies and configures ruff, black, isort, and pytest. The GitHub Actions CI workflow runs pre-commit, bandit, and pytest with coverage on every push and PR, enforcing the test-and-coverage discipline that CLAUDE.md from Step 1 mandates.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use `on` triggers to declare when they run, `jobs` for parallel units, and `steps` for sequential commands. Per the project's CLAUDE.md, CI is the authoritative test runner — local pytest is only for targeted debugging, and the full suite is verified by watching the `CI` workflow on every push.
